text.p: These are the stories making headlines in the Namibian newspapers today.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Workers on some communal farms in the far north are being paid starvation wages, and have to endure illegal working conditions, says labour inspector Selma Mweendobe.

- Namibia's lucrative livestock sector which has suffered a huge setback as a result of the drought will not show immediate signs of recovery despite an overall improvement in grazing conditions, says the Namibian Economic Policy Research Unit (NEPRU) in its latest quarterly review.

- Herero paramount chief Kuaima Riruako has sent a letter to the UN secretary-general Kofi Anan, in which he complains about violations of human and property rights by the SWAPO government regarding the Himba and Kxoe San people.

- With a verbal attack against the government a new party has announced its existence. The Namibia Movement for Independent Candidates (NMIC), headed by Joseph Kauendenge hopes to draw young people into politics.

- The Epupa saga and the continuing feud between groups that are for and against the project has taken a new turn with apparent attempts by government to find sponsorship for a pro-Epupa European trip, following the trip by Himba leaders opposed to the hydro-electric scheme.
